title: 2 Fast 2 Furious
full_review:
The street.car racing sequel, "2 Fast 2 Furious" (Universal), stalls and sputters as it depends on showy racing sequences to poorly disguise its empty shell of a script.

Paul Walker reprises his role as Brian from the original 2001 "The Fast and the Furious." In the sequel's plot, with holes wide enough to drive a Mack truck through, Brian is now a disgraced cop who squeaks out a living by illegally racing cars through the streets of Miami Beach. The original film became a huge hit among the male 18.24 (and younger) age group with its high.octane racing and fancy muscle cars.

It also launched the career of Vin Diesel, who now .. unfathomable as it may seem .. demands millions of dollars to star in any film. Diesel isn't in the sequel and has been replaced by singer.actor Tyrese, who plays opposite Walker, and who surely must have been willing to take less money for the role than Diesel.

Although there are still several scenes of cars piling up and one harrowing scene in which a car is smashed under the wheels of an 18.wheeler, the violence seems to have been toned down. However, women are still prancing around in tight, revealing clothes, pushed mainly into the background as arm candy for their male counterparts.

Despite the fueled car races with their hairpin turns and spin.outs, "2 Fast 2 Furious" is a yawner, unable to interest the audience in what is happening to the characters or produce more than mild excitement with its action scenes. Director John Singleton doesn't spend much time elaborating on why driving fast is such a thrill. His lackluster directing style seems to be saying, "It just is."

While the cars may be fast, the plot could have used some fuel injection. Brian has been recruited by the federal agents in Miami to collar Carter Verone (Cole Hauser), a money.laundering businessman who has been able to escape capture thus far. Brian pulls in his childhood friend Roman (Tyrese) to help him with the job. The incentive for the duo is that, if they are successful, their police records will be wiped clean. This is just one example of how screen writers Michael Brandt and Derek Haas cop out, going down a well.traveled road and borrowing characters and situations familiar from better movies. And just for good measure, beauty Eva Mendes plays an undercover cop romancing Carter in order to ensnare him.

The movie is an amateur effort with a big Hollywood budget, and it shows. It's flashy and fast, but otherwise void of any substance. Universal executives must be hoping that the original's popularity will help the dull sequel ride high for the opening weekend's box office. But it's likely to disappoint them beyond that point.

Because of brief violence and fisticuffs, dangerous illegal street car racing, a few passing sexual references, a flash of rear nudity and some crass language, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A.III .. adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG.13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
